findings.title: Test cleanup registers wrong alias (literal "alias") so created IDPs are never cleaned up
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` instead of using the actual alias variable (`alias` = "idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Consequence: the 21 IDPs created by this test are never removed by the cleanup (the cleanup targets a non-existent provider and may itself fail with 404), leaving the realm polluted and potentially causing cross-test interference and flaky failures for tests that count realm IDPs.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation can throw NPE when the login predicate evaluates a model with null config
findings.body: The new `getLoginPredicate()` in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter evaluates `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without a null guard on `getConfig()`. While `Objects::nonNull` guards the model itself, `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can return null for models constructed from representations/deserialization before `setConfig` is called. This predicate is invoked on every create() and remove() path (registerIDPLoginInvalidation), so a create/remove of an IDP whose config is null would throw a NullPointerException and abort the operation. A null-safe config access (e.g. `idp.getConfig() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`) is needed.

findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update compares organizationId but not BROKER_PUBLIC semantics of the fetch modes
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when the IDP qualifies for login before and after the update and `organizationId` is unchanged. However, for FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the delegate query filters on organizationId being null, while for ORG_ONLY/ALL with no specific organizationId it filters on BROKER_PUBLIC=true. If an IDP keeps the same organizationId but its BROKER_PUBLIC config changes in a way that keeps the predicate result unchanged while the set of cached queries it belongs to changes... more importantly, the predicate now treats a non-public org IDP (BROKER_PUBLIC=false) as not a login IDP, but the cached ORG_ONLY list keyed per searchKey may still legitimately contain org-linked IDPs in other states; the mismatch between the predicate-based invalidation decision and the actual delegate query criteria means there are update combinations (e.g. an IDP that is enabled and public before and after, but whose org linking via OrganizationProvider paths does not route through update()) where stale cached login lists are served. The invalidation logic should mirror the delegate's query filters exactly, and the organization unlink path (removing an IDP from an organization, which may bypass this provider's update()) needs an explicit invalidation of the login cache keys.

findings.title: getForLogin caches IDP lists per organizationId indefinitely, so new organizations' IDP links reuse stale entries without invalidation
findings.body: The login cache is keyed by (realm, FetchMode) with searchKey per organizationId. When an identity provider is linked to an organization through the OrganizationProvider (OrganizationManager.addIdentityProvider), Keycloak updates the IDP's organizationId via the storage provider, which is handled. However, when a new organization is created and IDPs are linked, the cache entry for searchKey "" (ORG_ONLY with organizationId=null, i.e. all org-linked public IDPs) is only invalidated if the IDP's predicate result flips. An IDP that is already public and org-linked (predicate passes) being moved from org A to org B keeps organizationId non-null on both sides only if the update is seen; but linking an already-public realm-level IDP to an org goes from organizationId=null to non-null, which is covered. The uncovered case: an IDP already linked to org A (passes predicate) gets linked to org B instead (organizationId changes) — this IS covered by the orgId comparison. The remaining gap is that the empty-string searchKey (ORG_ONLY, null org) aggregates across all organizations, and adding an IDP to a *new* organization where the IDP previously passed the predicate with the same organizationId is impossible, so the actual residual risk is operations performed through bulk/organization removal paths (org deletion cascades unlinking or deleting IDPs at the JPA level) that never invoke create/update/remove on this provider — those leave the cached login lists stale with IDs of deleted/unlinked IDPs. The getById-null fallback mitigates rendering but only per-request; the cache entry itself is never invalidated and is recomputed from a stale set on subsequent requests until something else invalidates the key.
